liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Alabama Getaway** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Played before any synth was added, though the Go to Heaven album was recorded that summer; Show is known for the first Alabama Getaway and for He's Gone [7][10][19]
- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): The jam coming out of it into He's Gone is sweet, and the jam after He's Gone too; Jams out of it feature Phil and Brent playing off each other [12][17]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Reviewer was surprised by the show opening with the reworked Minglewood arrangement [10]
- **Easy to Love You** (1 review): First performance of the song, which sounds fully formed, as if Brent brought it ready-made [15]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums are strong, with unusual sounds Brent added to the band's sound [12]
- **Space** (1 review): Reviewer describes the space as scary, leading into a post-drums Other One [17]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Other One super heavy [12]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Alabama Getaway [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-11-04.akgd200.friend.andrewf.101485.flac24** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 169 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Loud P.A. feedback in Minglewood from 4:37 to 5:08 was dampened with a narrow filter near 2.75kHz [1]
- **gd1979-11-04.sbd.macdonald.7919.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this soundboard transfer clean; A 30-second gap in Minglewood from the source CD was removed; cuts also affect Alabama Getaway, He's Gone and Around & Around [4][8]
- **gd1979-11-04.sbd.clugston.6947.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [7]. Said about its sound: There's a cut in He's Gone that is easy to miss on first listen; Soundboard has issues at the very start of Minglewood, so audience tapes are needed for the first seconds [11][19]
- **gd1979-11-04.akgd200.friend.andrewf.101486.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 169 min [2]

## Around the show

- Show came right after the Cape Cod, MA shows [10]
- Phil had only just started using an Irwin Tiger look-alike bass on this tour, giving a punchy tone [13]
- Brent plays a dynoed Rhodes piano on this tour [13]
- Played as the Iranian hostage situation was beginning [17]
- Greatest Story Ever Told returned at Keith and Donna's last show in February 1979 after nearly five years away; played regularly since [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-11-04.akgd200.friend.andrewf.101485.flac24**: taped by Tim Friend; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: AKG D200's > Technics RS-646DS (lead deck) > Sony TC-153SD (Tim's deck) > Maxell XL-II 90's. Mics on stand, set up behind the soundboard. [1]. Also: An alternate audience cassette of unknown lineage covers tape flips in He's Gone and Around & Around [1]
- **gd1979-11-04.sbd.macdonald.7919.shnf**: transferred by Alasdair Macdonald; source: SB>MR>Dick Latvala's cass>DAT>CD>EAC>minor editing>.shn & CD-R. [4]. Also: Earlier SB>MC>C>DAT>CD version circulated around 12/24/01; this transfer is a definite upgrade [4]
- **gd1979-11-04.sbd.clugston.6947.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > DAT> CDR [7]
- **gd1979-11-04.akgd200.friend.andrewf.101486.flac16**: taped by Tim Friend; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: AKG D200's > Technics RS-646DS (lead deck) > Sony TC-153SD (Tim's deck) > Maxell XL-II 90's. Mics on stand, set up behind the soundboard. [2]
